candidates.lead: Take-home pay in Queensland is worked out with federal ATO 2026-27 rates and the 2% Medicare levy; Queensland has no state income tax, so the same salary nets the same amount in Brisbane as in Perth. On the state's average full-time wage of $106,064 [[STATE_PROFILES.QLD.awote]], income tax is $22,339 and the Medicare levy $2,121, leaving $81,604 a year or $3,138.62 a fortnight [[calculatePayBreakdown]].

A pay calculator for QLD applies the same deductions as every other state — income tax at the 2026-27 resident rates, the 2% Medicare levy [[MEDICARE_LEVY.rate]] and any HECS-HELP repayment above $69,528 [[HECS_HELP.minimumThreshold]] — because there is no Queensland income tax. State-specific are the public holiday calendar, long service leave under the Industrial Relations Act, and payroll tax, which employers pay.

Queensland pay is gross salary less federal income tax and the Medicare levy, with 12% superannuation [[SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate]] paid by the employer on top. The average Queensland full-time adult earned $2,039.70 a week in May 2026 ([[STATE_PROFILES.QLD.awote]], ABS), or $106,064 a year, which takes home $81,604 under 2026-27 rates [[calculatePayBreakdown]], an effective tax rate of 23.1%.
